summary: Gradual queue entanglement in continuous batcher causing intermittent p95/p99 long-tail waves
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on a dedicated pool (NovaHealth) observed recurring p95/p99 latency waves and occasional 504s during sustained moderate traffic (20-40 qps) for chat endpoints. Spikes happen in a repeating pattern with ~7 minute periodicity and last ~30-90s. Impacts customer production workflows (document summarization pipelines) and triggers automated retries and billing anomalies.

Impact:
- Multiple requests for a single customer returning >2s p95 and >8s p99 during spikes; some connections eventually time out with 504.
- Affects NovaHealth's critical nightly ingest and real-time chat.
- Auto-retry from SDKs increased load and worsened tail during waves.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-nova-01 (us-west-2)
- Serving runtime: v1.21.3
- Continuous batcher config: linger=10ms, max_batch_tokens=4096, tenant_weighting=enabled
- KV cache: prefix-invalidation=periodic, warmup=enabled

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Send steady traffic at 25 qps with a mix of short (20 token) and medium (200 token) requests pinned to redwood-gpt-3.5-xl.
2. After ~4-8 minutes, p99 increases to 6-9s in a repeating wave pattern (spike -> recovery -> spike).
3. During spikes continuous-batcher CPU on a subset of nodes goes near 90% and a small fraction of long-lived streams show stalled flush events.

Relevant logs (excerpt):
- continuous-batcher: "flush_delay=78ms tenant=tenant-nova queue_len=34 reason=entangled-prefix"
- serving-runtime: "kv-cache: hit_ratio=0.83 stale_prefixes=12"
- api-gateway: "upstream_timeout 504 path=/v1/chat/stream tenant=nova request_id..."

Customer notes: "We see periodic slowdowns every few minutes that line up with our ingest batches; when we reduce parallelism the problem lessens but throughput drops."
comments: 2026-03-08 | Priya Nair (Support): Triage: Customer reported p99 waves and 504s starting 2026-03-07 22:00 UTC. Assigned to SRE for deeper investigation.

2026-03-09 | Rafael Ortiz (SRE): Initial checks: node-level CPU and queue metrics show correlated resource pressure on a small subset of pod replicas; no obvious OOMs. Added continuous-batcher debug logging. Asked customer for SDK log bundle.
2026-03-10 | NovaHealth (Customer): Provided SDK logs and reproduction script. Noted that spikes align with their ingest batch windows. Asked whether model pinning could cause hot-sharding.

2026-03-11 | Rafael Ortiz (SRE): Observed periodic lockstep flushes: several tenant queues appear to align their timers and cause simultaneous flushes, creating short-lived overload. Hypothesis: stale prefix kv-cache invalidation combined with tenant-weighted coalescing causes 'queue entanglement'.
2026-03-12 | Ava Chen (Platform Eng): Running canary of a mitigation that randomizes batcher flush offsets and increases per-tenant jitter. Will collect 24h of metrics before recommending rollout.
2026-03-12 | Priya Nair (Support): Notified customer of ongoing mitigation test and provided temporary workaround: lower client-side parallelism to reduce impact until fix is validated.
investigation_notes: Metric correlation: p99 spikes line up with spikes in continuous-batcher pending queue length and a subset of worker CPU pegging. No increase in total traffic that explains the magnitude—suggests internal synchronization.

Hypothesis A: Periodic KV-cache invalidation (prefix rotation) triggers cache warmups which temporarily increase per-request token processing; combined with batcher flush alignment this produces waves.

Hypothesis B: Tenant-weighted coalescing adjustment recently rolled (runtime v1.21.2->v1.21.3) introduced deterministic flush timers that can drift into lockstep across tenants with similar request patterns.
Experiment: Deployed debug build toggling 'batcher_flush_jitter' on dp-nova-01 and observed immediate smoothing of p95/p99 tails in canary nodes for 6h window.
Logs: Found repeated "stalled_flush" messages tied to requests that held KV read locks for longer than expected (50-120ms). This increased batch wait time and amplified coalescing latency.

Cross-check: Linked to past incident SUP-27654 which described cross-tenant batch merging; this case differs because the failure mode is periodic lockstep induced by cache invalidation + deterministic timer behavior.
Temporary mitigation applied: enabled per-replica batcher jitter and raised max_concurrent_streams limit for affected nodes to reduce head-of-line blocking.
Monitoring: Added dashboard panels for per-tenant flush-timestamp histograms, stale-prefix counts, and batcher_pending_len across replicas.
resolution:
Workaround and planned fix:
- Short term: Instructed NovaHealth to temporarily reduce client concurrency and applied per-replica batcher flush jitter on their dedicated pool. This reduced p99 spikes by ~80% in canary.
- Medium term: Engineering change to introduce randomized flush offsets and make prefix-invalidation asynchronous to avoid synchronized KV warmups. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1427 (in review).
- Postmortem actions: Update continuous-batcher runbook to include detection and automatic jitter enablement, instrument per-tenant stalled_flush alerts, and schedule a config rollout for all dedicated pools after verification.
Status: Canary mitigation showing positive results; target full rollout after 72h validation. Customer notified and accepted workaround.
